items.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Then eventually I got to play there with Maynard... I played this stuff with Maynard... when I was with Maynard, the payroll was 120 a week

ctx.x: Now it’s around 1950, you started playing, you got into Birdland in New York City?

Birdland came after I left, when we left Washington, D.C. When the lady didn’t pay the taxes, we all split up. Then I started to — through somebody I knew, so I knew the manager of Birdland so I got to play in Birdland, I started playing in Birdland, right. I have pictures of that with, I used to play Monday nights, battle of the saxophones, Eddie “Lockjaw” Davis and myself and I played there Monday night with Art Blakey and all © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

the groups. And then I did two weeks with the Kai Winding group, we did two whole weeks. I’ve got pictures, not here, which I’ll show you later when you want. In the group was Zoot Sims, myself, Joe Newman, Billy Taylor, Kai Winding was the leader, Don Lamond, Clyde Lombardi and that was it. We were two weeks, it was just fantastic. Then eventually I got to play there with Maynard. Because Maynard, we were the busiest of all. Maynard and the Miles Davis group, we were sharing the bandstand, an hour each. And…
